qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507.mistake: The FOL statement p_6(Darling) → p_7(Darling) says that *if Darling is hermaphroditic, then it self-fertilizes*. However, being hermaphroditic does not necessarily imply self-fertilization; it only means the organism has both male and female reproductive organs. The natural language statement incorrectly assumes a necessary causal link from being hermaphroditic to self-fertilizing, which is not logically valid. The FOL implication makes a strong, unwarranted claim that every hermaphrodite *does* self-fertilize, whereas in biological contexts, hermaphroditism allows for self-fertilization but does not entail it. Thus, the FOL does not correctly correspond to a reasonable interpretation of the NL without assuming more than the biology supports. Therefore, this mapping is misleading and incorrect in a logical modeling context.

openai/gpt-5-mini.mistake: The NL phrase “can either … or …” was rendered as a strict implication forcing an exclusive truth (p_6 → (p_7 ⊕ p_0)). The NL implies possibility/ability (may have either trait), not that a hermaphrodite must in fact have exactly one of those properties. This is a modal/strength mismatch.
